messages:
customer_acme: Hey, we're seeing a wave of requests that should be routed to eu-west-1 hitting us-east-1 yesterday around 15:05-15:20 UTC. p95 latency +220ms for our users and an unexpected billing spike. Also observed intermittent 401s. sample req ids: req_aa1, req_bb2

emma-support: sorry about that. can you paste the X-Redwood-Trace / X-Region-Pref headers and a sample cookie? timeframe ok — we'll triage.

customer_acme: timeframe 2024-11-29 15:05-15:20 UTC. Header: X-Region-Pref: eu-west-1, X-Request-ID: req_aa1. Cookie seen on client: rw_route=eu-west-1|prio=0|wt=70|ts=1700000000. We didn't change routing policy.

raj-infra: interesting — cookie shows ttl semantics weirdness? can you paste the actual Set-Cookie string (full)? also did you change failover policy via console recently?

customer_acme: full cookie we captured: rw_route=eu-west-1|prio=0|wt=70|ts=1700000000; Path=/; HttpOnly. No manual edits on our side.

li-devoncall: taking over for repro. steps I used:
curl -H "Cookie: rw_route=eu-west-1|prio=0|wt=70|ts=1700000000" \n  -H "X-Region-Pref: eu-west-1" -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate

li-devoncall: local trace output when I hit canary: 
```
route_eval: available=[eu-west-1,us-east-1]
policy_serialized=[{"priority":1,"weight":30},{"priority":0,"weight":70}]
backend_order_after_sort=[us-east-1,eu-west-1]
selected_region=us-east-1 reason=priority_sorting
cookie_present=true cookie_ttl=0
```

li-devoncall: tl;dr the UI-saved priority array appears to be stored latest-first but the backend sorts ascending, so effective order flipped. also cookie_ttl logged as 0 (expired).

raj-infra: also found a secondary parser bug — weights with fractional values (e.g., "0.5") are parsed as int in legacy parser and become 0, which changes tie-break behavior. filed as INF-4382.

maria-product: is the ttl unit mismatch known? product UI shows TTL field as "seconds" in tooltip but console migration in 2024-11 treated it as milliseconds in storage in one migration step. that explains ttl=1 -> stored 1ms -> cookie expired immediately on next request.

emma-support: the 401s make sense now: auth verification is regional. when a request hits us-east it validates against a different key set and returns 401 for tokens minted for eu-west. the routing flip caused auth errors for a subset of sessions.

raj-infra: repro config I used: 
```
failover_policy: {
  "regions": ["eu-west-1","us-east-1"],
  "priorities": [1,0],
  "weights": [30,70],
  "sticky_ttl": 1
}
```
Backend interpreted sticky_ttl as ms here -> effectively zero. Also backend sorted priorities, resulting in us-east selected.

li-devoncall: quick mitigation plan:
- update backend parser to *not* auto-sort priority arrays, respect explicit order (patch in flight)
- treat sticky_ttl as seconds for backward compat until UI is fixed (hotfix)
- add defensive migration that converts existing stored TTLs that look like ms to seconds when value <= 1000

deploy-bot: Deploy started: patch/priority-and-ttl-fix -> canary 10% -> 2 nodes (build 2024.11.30-rc2)

raj-infra: found an additional UX wrinkle: the console edit flow saves arrays with newest-first, which reversed user-specified order when they edited any element. we'll add an explicit index field display and a migration to preserve ordering.

emma-support: customer, short-term we can backfill your users by issuing Set-Cookie: rw_route=eu-west-1; Max-Age=86400; Path=/ so sessions stick to EU for 24h while we roll patches. want us to push that?

billing-team: billing spike reason analysis: the fallback to us-east triggered on-demand pricing and egress differences. if you provide exact invoice ids/time window we can calculate credit.

customer_acme: please do backfill, and I'll DM invoice ids now. thanks — big relief. :thumbsup: 

li-devoncall: canary looks good so far, latency normalizing and 401s dropping. I'll monitor for 30m then promote.

deploy-bot: Canary success -> promoted to 100% in 12m.

maria-product: follow-ups for backlog: add unit tests for weight parsing, UI tooltip for TTL units, console migration audit and RN entry. created ticket PROD-9123.

emma-support: closing the loop — we'll confirm credit and that your metrics look normal later today. thanks for the quick reports and patience :white_check_mark:
